name: Turbinate reduction

angle.text: Users look at turbinate reduction as a companion to septoplasty or rhinoplasty, so the nose both breathes well and can be reshaped. It is a functional operation rather than a cosmetic one, and forum posters debate its trade-offs, including empty nose syndrome. Evidence covers airway outcomes, not appearance.

summary: Surgery that shrinks enlarged inferior turbinates to improve nasal breathing; a functional procedure with many techniques and limited high-quality comparisons.
note: Mainly a breathing procedure, not a cosmetic one; some forum posters warn about empty nose syndrome after aggressive reduction.
currentQuick:
Turbinates are folds of tissue inside the nose that warm and humidify air. When the inferior turbinates are enlarged they can block airflow, and turbinate reduction is the surgical family of methods used to shrink them. It is often paired with septoplasty or rhinoplasty.
In looksmaxxing forums it comes up in breathing-focused threads, usually alongside jaw and palate expansion, where members disagree about whether reduction is the right fix and discuss fear of over-resection.
How it works: Techniques include removing tissue (turbinectomy), cautery by electric, laser or radiofrequency methods, cryotherapy, and submucosal resection, with or without moving the bone outward. A review counted at least 13 techniques used over 130 years.
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe a serious lack of well-designed comparative studies. The goal in the literature is to reduce symptoms while preserving turbinate function. Forum members cite empty nose syndrome as a concern; its status is debated among clinicians and it is not assessed in the sources reviewed here.
deepLead:
Turbinate reduction is a group of surgical procedures that reduce the size of the inferior turbinates, the mucosa-covered structures on the side walls of the nasal cavity, to relieve nasal obstruction. It is often combined with septoplasty or rhinoplasty because enlargement can occur on the side opposite a deviated septum, described as compensatory hypertrophy.
A review of techniques counted at least 13 methods over 130 years and reported a serious lack of qualified studies, with prospective randomised comparisons being extremely rare. Its authors stated that the purpose of surgery should be to reduce complaints while preserving turbinate function. A later randomised trial of 382 patients compared six techniques over six years of follow-up.
In looksmaxxing communities the procedure is discussed mostly as a breathing intervention and compared with maxillary expansion, with some members warning against aggressive reduction.

name: Nasal valve repair

angle.text: Nasal valve repair is discussed by people planning rhinoplasty who want a nose that is both well shaped and open for breathing, since a collapsing valve can narrow the sidewalls. It is a functional rhinoplasty technique studied mainly in case series reporting airway improvement.

summary: Functional surgery to widen or support the narrowest part of the nasal airway when it collapses; the literature is mostly case series with improvements reported.
note: A breathing operation first; appearance changes can accompany it.
currentQuick:
The nasal valve is the narrowest part of the nasal airway. When its walls are weak or narrow, the nostrils can collapse inward on inhalation. Nasal valve repair covers surgical ways of supporting or widening it, often with cartilage grafts or sutures.
It appears in looksmaxxing discussion mainly as a breathing fix that overlaps with nose shaping.
How it works: Surgeons typically add structural support, for example spreader or batten-type grafts, or use minimally invasive implants, sometimes alongside septoplasty and turbinate surgery. Diagnosis often involves the Cottle manoeuvre, though its accuracy has been questioned.
Risks and caveats: A 25-year systematic review found supportive evidence for valve surgery but limited by study quality. Complications are those of nasal surgery in general, including persisting obstruction and the possibility of revision.
deepLead:
Nasal valve repair refers to surgical techniques that treat obstruction caused by compromise of the nasal valve, the narrow region of the airway at the junction of the upper lateral cartilage, septum and turbinate. It is a form of functional rhinoplasty.
A 25-year systematic review of the English-language literature examined the evidence for modern techniques and concluded on the basis of the studies it found that the topic had supporting data, with limits in study design. A retrospective series of 53 consecutive patients assessed causes, efficacy and cosmetic effect of reconstruction.
The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum discussion of this procedure, so community views are not documented here.

name: Ultrasonic (piezo) rhinoplasty

angle.text: Piezo rhinoplasty is promoted as a way to reshape the nasal bones precisely, with a straighter or lower bridge as the visible result. The reshaping is visible once swelling settles. Evidence for its advantages over chisels and rasps is mostly descriptive, from surgeon reviews.

summary: Nose surgery that reshapes bone with piezoelectric ultrasonic tools instead of chisels and rasps; evidence is thin and mostly descriptive.
note: Few published comparisons; sources reviewed here are a technique overview and two registered trials.
currentQuick:
Ultrasonic or piezo rhinoplasty uses instruments driven by piezoelectric vibration to cut and shape the nasal bones. Proponents describe more precise bone cuts and less collateral damage than hand chisels.
It is introduced in the literature as a bone-sculpting tool within otherwise standard rhinoplasty and is used in dorsal preservation work as well.
How it works: The instruments vibrate at ultrasonic frequency and cut bone while sparing soft tissue. A technique overview says they allow precise osteotomies under direct visual control after an open or extended closed approach, plus ostectomies and rhinosculpture.
Risks and caveats: The sources reviewed describe technique rather than comparative harms. A registered trial compares piezo with endonasal osteotomy on postoperative healing, and results are not available in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Ultrasonic rhinoplasty is a way of performing the bone work of rhinoplasty using piezoelectric instruments designed for the purpose. A 2023 review of ultrasonic rhinoplasty and septoplasty states that the instruments allow precise osteotomies under direct visual control after an open or extended closed approach, as well as ostectomies and rhinosculpture, and that they preserve bone stability by not damaging support structures and avoiding unwanted fractures.
A general rhinoplasty reference dates the introduction of ultrasonic rhinoplasty to 2004 and credits it to Massimo Robiony; it describes the devices as similar to those used in dental surgery and sparing of soft tissue.
Published comparative evidence in the sources reviewed is limited to a registered trial comparing piezo and endonasal osteotomy.

name: Preservation rhinoplasty

angle.text: Preservation rhinoplasty is sought by people who want a smaller dorsal hump or a straighter profile while keeping their natural bridge lines. The visible profile change is the goal of the operation itself. Surgeon reports are mostly case series, with claims of favourable aesthetic results.

summary: Nose surgery that lowers or reshapes the bridge while keeping the natural dorsal structure intact rather than cutting a hump off; popular among surgeons, with mostly case-series evidence.
note: Hump recurrence and technique-specific problems are discussed in the literature; evidence is largely retrospective.
currentQuick:
Preservation rhinoplasty is an approach in which the surgeon keeps the nose's original bony and cartilaginous bridge and lowers it as a unit, instead of the traditional method of cutting off a dorsal hump. The term was coined by Daniel in 2018, according to a case-series paper.
Surgical authors describe it as a shift in philosophy, with claims of better aesthetic and functional results that are still being tested.
How it works: The osseocartilaginous vault is mobilised as a single unit and pushed down or let down (push-down and let-down techniques), preserving natural dorsal lines and mucosa. Several classification systems and hybrid approaches have been proposed.
Risks and caveats: Reported problems include hump recurrence after let-down or push-down surgery. Evidence in the sources reviewed comprises retrospective series, a radiological comparison with hump resection, and registered trials.
deepLead:
Preservation rhinoplasty, also called dorsal preservation rhinoplasty, refers to techniques that address a dorsal hump or the nasal profile by repositioning rather than removing the natural dorsum. A 2020 review notes a rekindled interest in dorsal preservation as an alternative to conventional hump resection, with claims of superior functional and aesthetic results, and describes mobilising the osseocartilaginous vault as a single unit to avoid disrupting natural structure.
A 2018 article titled as a rhinoplasty revolution popularised the term, and a 2020 case series states that the term was coined by Daniel in 2018 and represents a fundamental change in philosophy. Later papers proposed classification systems, hybrid structural approaches and guidelines.
The evidence base consists of retrospective series and comparisons; no large randomised trial is present in the sources reviewed.

name: Revision rhinoplasty

angle.text: Revision rhinoplasty is discussed by people unhappy with a first nose job who want shape or breathing problems corrected, often with cartilage grafts. The corrected shape is visible after healing. Revision rates of roughly 5 to 20 percent are documented in surgical references.

summary: A second (or later) operation to correct problems from a previous nose job; revision rates are documented and the procedure often needs grafts.
note: Technically more complex than primary surgery; body dysmorphic disorder symptoms are common in people seeking rhinoplasty.
currentQuick:
Revision rhinoplasty is surgery to fix aesthetic or functional problems after a previous rhinoplasty, such as tip drop, asymmetry, collapse or breathing difficulty. Wikipedia puts the share of primary operations needing revision at 5 to 20 percent.
On looksmax.org, members ask whether a drooping tip a year after surgery needs a full redo or a minor closed procedure, and discuss other factors such as jaw support.
How it works: Revisions are usually done by an open approach and often require cartilage from the ear or rib, or implants. Literature covers conchal cartilage grafts for valve collapse, irradiated costal cartilage, Gore-Tex, porous polyethylene and silicone implants.
Risks and caveats: Reports describe complications from implants and graft materials, persisting obstruction, and dissatisfaction. A study of rhinoplasty candidates found high prevalence of body dysmorphic disorder symptoms.
deepLead:
Revision rhinoplasty, or secondary rhinoplasty, is a nose operation performed after a previous rhinoplasty to address aesthetic or functional problems. A general reference gives 5 to 20 percent as the share of primary operations needing a second procedure and lists typical problems such as breathing deficits, asymmetry, collapse, a hanging columella, a pinched tip and a scooped nose. A study of a plastic surgery group practice examined cosmetic rhinoplasty revision rates and risk factors for dissatisfaction.
Revision surgery commonly uses open approaches and cartilage grafts or implants, and the literature includes long-term series on Gore-Tex, porous high-density polyethylene, irradiated homologous costal cartilage and silicone implants. A review of risks and complications describes the range of problems after rhinoplasty.
In looksmaxxing communities it appears in individual cases where a member asks about a tip that dropped after surgery.

name: Alar base reduction (alarplasty)

angle.text: Alarplasty is used to narrow wide nostrils or a broad nose base, usually alongside rhinoplasty, and the narrower base is visible once healed. Forum posters debate how much change a given face needs. Trial evidence specific to alarplasty is limited.

summary: Surgery that trims the nostril flare; usually done alongside a nose job, with little trial evidence of its own.
note: Alters the nostril opening, so airflow effects have been studied; most literature is technique reports.
currentQuick:
Alar base reduction is a small cosmetic surgery that removes tissue near the nostril wing to make the nostrils narrower or less flared. It is most often combined with rhinoplasty.
On looksmaxxing forums it appears mostly in before-and-after photo threads. Published research is mainly technique descriptions and classification studies rather than trials of how much it improves appearance.
How it works: Small wedges of skin and soft tissue are removed from the nostril sill or the alar-facial junction and the wound is closed, reducing nostril width.
Risks and caveats: As a surgical change to the nostril opening, it has been studied for effects on breathing, and some functional nasal surgery reports link nostril reduction to airflow concerns. Scarring and asymmetry are general surgical concerns; no controlled trials of cosmetic outcomes were found.
deepLead:
Alar base reduction, usually called alarplasty, is a cosmetic nasal surgery that narrows the width of the nostril flare or the base of the nose by removing small wedges of tissue at the nostril rim or the alar-facial junction. It is performed either on its own or together with rhinoplasty, and surgeons describe it as one of several tools for correcting nostril size and shape.
In looksmaxxing culture it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option for people who consider their nostrils too wide or flared. Published literature on the topic consists mainly of surgical technique descriptions and classification studies, including work on how the alar region moves during a smile, rather than controlled trials of cosmetic satisfaction.

name: Tip plasty / cartilage grafting

angle.text: Tip plasty is used to refine a bulbous, drooping or under-projected nasal tip with sutures, cartilage trimming or grafts, and the new tip shape is visible after healing. It is described as a technically demanding part of rhinoplasty and is supported by technique papers rather than large trials.

summary: Surgical reshaping of the nose tip with sutures and cartilage grafts; an established rhinoplasty step backed by technique papers, not large trials.
note: Revision rhinoplasty is reported in roughly 5-20% of nose surgeries overall.
currentQuick:
Tip plasty reshapes or supports the end of the nose, using sutures, trimming or cartilage grafts, typically taken from the septum, ear or rib. It is aimed at bulbous, wide or underprojected tips.
The surgical literature is extensive but mostly technique descriptions and retrospective series, with a few small trials of specific graft or strut methods.
How it works: Surgeons alter the tip cartilages with stitches, add grafts that change contour or projection, or reposition the cartilage, often through an open approach.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia reports that secondary rhinoplasty occurs in roughly 5-20% of operations, and tip or dorsal irregularities are among the reasons. Graft complications, including those of septal extension grafts in Asian patients, have been documented in case series.
deepLead:
Tip plasty (nasal tip refinement) is the part of rhinoplasty that reshapes, repositions or supports the nasal tip, using cartilage sutures, cartilage excision or cartilage grafts. It is generally described as one of the technically more demanding parts of nose surgery.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as the surgical route for a bulbous, wide or underprojected tip. The surgical literature on tip work is large and mostly consists of technique papers and retrospective series; a handful of small registered trials compare specific tip-support techniques.

name: Rib cartilage graft rhinoplasty

angle.text: Rib cartilage grafts are discussed by people who need substantial structural material for major nose rebuilds, such as dorsal reconstruction or revision surgery, using their own tissue. The rebuilt shape is visible after healing. Evidence comes mainly from surgical case series.

summary: Uses the patient's own rib cartilage for big structural rebuilds of the nose; supported by surgical case series.
note: Requires a second surgical site on the chest; donor site morbidity is assessed in studies.
currentQuick:
Rib cartilage rhinoplasty uses cartilage taken from the patient's rib to build or support the nose when the septum cannot supply enough. It is commonly discussed for major dorsal work and revisions.
Evidence comes from retrospective series, including a 58-patient cohort reporting stable results.
How it works: Cartilage is harvested from the rib, carved into grafts such as dorsal onlays or columellar struts, and placed in the nose.
Risks and caveats: The procedure adds a chest donor site, and studies track donor site morbidity, graft warping and revision need. Details beyond the cited cohort were not reviewed.
deepLead:
Rib (costal) cartilage graft rhinoplasty is a form of nose surgery in which cartilage harvested from the patient's own ribs is carved into grafts to support or build up the nose. It is used when a large amount of structural material is needed, for example in major dorsal reconstruction or revision surgery.
In looksmaxxing discussion it appears as the structural-support option within hardmaxxing nose surgery. Published evidence consists of retrospective surgical series.

name: Silicone/Gore-Tex nasal implant

angle.text: Silicone and Gore-Tex implants are used to raise a low nasal bridge, particularly in Asian rhinoplasty, as an alternative to the patient's own cartilage. The added bridge height is immediately visible. The literature consists mainly of surgical series and comparisons.

summary: Synthetic bridge implants for low noses, long used in Asian rhinoplasty, with cartilage as the main alternative.
note: Evidence here is reviews and case series; patients may not be suitable for or accept synthetic materials.
currentQuick:
Silicone and Gore-Tex implants are synthetic materials placed in the nose to raise a low bridge. Reviews describe a long history of alloplastic implant use in Asia.
The alternative is the patient's own cartilage, such as rib, which has its own complication profile.
How it works: A carved implant is placed along the nasal dorsum to increase height.
Risks and caveats: Reviews say some patients are unsuitable for or decline alloplastic materials; Wikipedia says autologous grafts carry less rejection risk. Specific complication rates for silicone and Gore-Tex were not reviewed here.
deepLead:
Silicone and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (Gore-Tex) nasal implants are synthetic (alloplastic) materials placed in the nose, most often to raise a low nasal bridge. They are an alternative to the patient's own cartilage and are particularly associated in the literature with augmentation rhinoplasty in Asian patients.
Reviews describe a long history of alloplastic implant use in Asia, while noting that some patients are unsuitable for or decline synthetic materials and that costal cartilage is an alternative. In looksmaxxing forums, nose-job outcomes in Asian patients are a recurring topic.

name: Septal extension graft

angle.text: A septal extension graft is used in rhinoplasty to set the tip's position, projection and rotation, especially when the lower lateral cartilages are weak. The tip change is visible after healing. It is an established technique, with comparative data growing.

summary: A cartilage graft that extends the septum to control nose-tip length, projection and rotation; established technique with growing comparative data.
note: Complications have been reported in Asian patients; trials against columellar struts are ongoing.
currentQuick:
A septal extension graft attaches cartilage to the end of the septum so the surgeon can set the tip's position, length and rotation. It is used mostly for weak or underprojected tips.
Wikipedia says it gives more control and changes less than a columellar strut; a 2019 cohort compared the two.
How it works: Cartilage, usually harvested from the septum, is fixed to the caudal septum, creating a stable platform for the tip cartilages.
Risks and caveats: A 2014 study reported complications of the graft in Asian patients. As with other rhinoplasty, revision surgery can be needed.
deepLead:
A septal extension graft is a piece of cartilage, usually from the septum, attached to the end of the nasal septum in rhinoplasty to control the position, length, projection and rotation of the nasal tip. It is used particularly in patients with weak lower lateral cartilages.
In looksmaxxing discussion it is associated with lengthening or rotating the nose tip. The evidence is surgical case series, comparative cohort studies and several registered trials.

name: PDO nose thread lift

angle.text: PDO thread lifts are promoted as a non-surgical way to raise the nasal bridge or tip, sometimes combined with filler, with the lift visible soon after treatment. The result is temporary as the threads absorb. Published evidence is very limited.

summary: Absorbable threads placed in the nose to lift bridge or tip without surgery; very little published evidence.
note: Evidence is one case-based review and a 10-person registered trial.
currentQuick:
PDO nose threads are dissolvable threads inserted into the nose, sometimes with filler, as a non-surgical way to change bridge or tip shape.
The published evidence is thin.
How it works: Absorbable polydioxanone threads are placed under the skin to add support and volume.
Risks and caveats: A 2024 review discusses adverse effects of nose thread procedures and prevention methods; details of their frequency were not reviewed here.
deepLead:
A PDO nose thread lift is a minimally invasive, non-surgical rhinoplasty procedure in which absorbable polydioxanone (PDO) threads are inserted under the skin of the nose, sometimes together with filler, to raise the bridge or tip.
Published literature is sparse: a 2024 review of clinical cases in Skin Research and Technology and one small registered trial.

name: Botox nose tip lift

angle.text: Proponents use botulinum toxin in the depressor septi nasi muscle as a short-term way to lift a drooping tip, especially one that drops when smiling. It is an off-label use with temporary results, and no published trials have tested it.

summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the muscle that pulls the nasal tip down; a temporary, off-label tip lift with no published trials behind it.
note: Off-label use of a prescription toxin; effects are temporary and no trials were found.
currentQuick:
A Botox nose tip lift relaxes the depressor septi nasi, a small muscle that tugs the nasal tip downward. Proponents say this lets a drooping tip sit a little higher, especially when smiling.
The effect is described as temporary, lasting as long as the toxin does, usually a few months. No clinical trials of the nasal tip use were found.
How it works: Botulinum toxin blocks the signal from nerve to muscle, weakening the targeted muscle for a period of months. Weakening the depressor septi nasi reduces its downward pull on the tip.
Risks and caveats: Botulinum toxin is prescription-only. Reported cosmetic adverse effects include weakness of nearby muscles, headache and allergic reactions, and the FDA has issued warnings about toxin spreading beyond the injection site. The nasal use is off-label.
deepLead:
A Botox nose tip lift is a cosmetic procedure in which botulinum toxin is injected into the depressor septi nasi muscle, a small muscle that pulls the nasal tip and the base of the nostrils downward, in order to relax it and allow the tip of the nose to sit slightly higher. It is sometimes grouped with other non-surgical nose treatments and is described by its proponents as a short-term alternative to surgery for a drooping tip, particularly one that drops further when a person smiles or speaks.
The depressor septi nasi originates near the upper jaw and inserts into the nasal septum and the alar part of the nasalis muscle; it also moves the nasal tip when the upper lip moves. Botulinum toxin products are prescription-only in the United States, UK and EU, and their effects are reported to last roughly two to four months, sometimes up to six.
The nasal tip use is an off-label application: regulatory approvals for cosmetic botulinum toxin concern glabellar (frown) lines, and the sources reviewed for this entry describe no approved labelling for the nose. No clinical trials of nasal tip injection were located for this article, so the effect size and duration of the procedure are documented here only as practitioner claims.

name: Nose contouring makeup

chain: Dark shade on sides, light on bridge
angle.text: Contouring makeup is used to make the nose look slimmer, straighter or more defined for the day, and the optical effect is visible straight away and washes off. It applies general contouring methods to the nose, and no studies have tested it specifically.

summary: Shading and highlighting to make the nose look slimmer; purely optical, reversible and untested in studies.
note: Temporary visual effect only; no studies of its perceived effect were found.
currentQuick:
Nose contouring uses a darker shade on the sides of the nose and a lighter one on the bridge or tip to create the illusion of a slimmer, straighter nose.
It is an established makeup technique with roots in theatre and film, popularized more widely in the 2010s.
How it works: Dark shades recede and light shades advance visually, so shading along the sides of the nose can make it look narrower. Nothing about the underlying structure changes.
Risks and caveats: Risks are those of ordinary cosmetics, such as skin irritation or breakouts in sensitive individuals. The effect disappears when the makeup is removed.
deepLead:
Nose contouring is a makeup technique in which a darker shade is applied along the sides of the nose and a lighter shade on the bridge or tip, with the aim of making the nose look slimmer, straighter or more defined through light and shadow. It is a specific application of contouring, defined as using cosmetics to define, enhance and sculpt facial structure.
The practice changes only the visual impression of the nose while the makeup is worn and does not alter its structure. It is widely discussed alongside non-surgical and surgical nose changes as the lowest-commitment option, and is used both in everyday makeup and in stage, film and drag makeup.

name: Nasal taping at night

angle.text: Social-media users wear micropore or kinesiology tape on the nose overnight as a non-surgical mini nose job for a slimmer or lifted look. Claims of gradual cartilage remodelling are anecdotal, and surgeons describe any effect as fading when the tape is removed.

summary: Micropore or kinesiology tape worn on the nose overnight for a slimmer look; surgeons say any effect vanishes when the tape comes off.
note: Skin irritation and tape-removal damage are the main reported risks.
currentQuick:
Nasal taping means wearing adhesive tape on the nose for hours or overnight to create a slimmer or more lifted look. It spread on TikTok in the early 2020s.
Plastic surgeons quoted in coverage say any change lasts only while the tape is worn. No clinical trials of the cosmetic use were found.
How it works: The tape presses on the skin and soft tissue of the nose, which can change its appearance while worn. Bone and cartilage are not altered.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks are skin irritation, contact dermatitis, breakouts and skin damage on removal, mainly in sensitive skin. Doctors quoted advise checking first if there are breathing problems.
deepLead:
Nasal taping is a social-media trend in which people apply adhesive tape, commonly micropore paper tape or kinesiology tape, across the bridge and sides of the nose for several hours or overnight in an attempt to create a slimmer, more lifted or more defined nose. It is often marketed as a non-surgical mini nose job.
Grokipedia reports that the trend grew on TikTok from the early 2020s and gained wide visibility in 2023 and 2024, and that plastic surgeons say taping cannot permanently reshape the nose, with any visible change lasting only while the tape is worn. The technique borrows from taping used after rhinoplasty to manage swelling. No clinical trials of cosmetic nose taping were located.

name: Nose-lifting or slimming massage

angle.text: Beauty communities describe daily nose rubbing or pinching as a free, non-surgical way to slim or lift the nose. The claimed reshaping rests on anecdote, and no studies have tested it.

summary: Daily nose rubbing or pinching claimed to slim or lift the nose; no studies have tested it.
note: No studies found; surgeons say shape is set by bone and cartilage.
currentQuick:
Nose massage is the practice of rubbing or pressing the nose, often daily, in the hope of slimming or lifting it.
No published studies were found that test the practice.
How it works: Proponents say repeated pressure gradually reshapes the nose. Surgeons quoted about similar pressure methods say bone and cartilage are not changed by outside pressure.
Risks and caveats: No documented harms specific to the practice were found. General skin irritation from frequent rubbing is possible.
deepLead: Nose-lifting or slimming massage refers to the practice of pressing, pinching or rubbing the nose, often daily, with the aim of making it narrower, higher-bridged or more lifted. It is described in beauty and appearance communities as a no-cost, non-surgical option.

name: Nose exercises (nose yoga)

angle.text: Nose exercises, part of face yoga, are promoted to strengthen nasal muscles and change nostril or tip shape through flaring, scrunching and pressing. The reshaping claim rests on anecdote, and no studies have tested it.

summary: Nostril flaring and nose scrunching routines claimed to reshape the nose; no studies have tested them.
note: No studies found.
currentQuick:
Nose exercises are muscle routines such as nostril flaring that proponents say can slim the nostrils or lift the tip.
No published studies were found on whether they change nose shape.
How it works: Proponents say exercising the small muscles around the nose changes its shape. The nose's main structure is bone and cartilage, which these muscles do not directly reshape.
Risks and caveats: No documented harms specific to the practice were found.
deepLead: Nose exercises, sometimes called nose yoga, are routines of flaring the nostrils, wiggling or scrunching the nose, or pressing on the tip, promoted as a way to strengthen nasal muscles and change the shape of the nostrils or nasal tip. They belong to the wider category of facial exercise or face yoga.

name: Buteyko breathing

chain: Better breathing habits, claimed facial benefit
angle.text: Buteyko is a breathing-retraining method that users in looksmaxxing circles connect with nasal breathing, mouth taping and the idea that breathing habits shape the face. Trials in asthma show modest symptom effects, and none test facial appearance.

summary: A breathing-retraining method built around nasal, reduced breathing; asthma trials show modest symptom effects and none test it for looks.
note: Studied for asthma only; claims about appearance are untested.
currentQuick:
The Buteyko method teaches nasal, reduced breathing and relaxation, based on the theory that chronic over-breathing drives conditions such as asthma. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the 1950s.
Trials in asthma suggest possible symptom and quality-of-life benefits with little change in lung function. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed alongside nasal breathing and mouth taping, but no studies test it for appearance.
How it works: Practitioners aim to reduce breathing volume, breathe through the nose and relax, tracking progress with a breath-hold time called the control pause.
Risks and caveats: The sources reviewed describe no specific adverse events. Medical commentators object to broad claims, such as reduced medication use, that lack adequate evidence.
deepLead:
The Buteyko method is a breathing retraining system developed by Ukrainian physiologist Konstantin Buteyko in the Soviet Union in the 1950s. Its three principles are nasal breathing, reduced breathing, and relaxation, and it is based on the theory that chronic over-breathing (hyperventilation) causes or worsens conditions such as asthma.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to encourage nasal breathing, calm anxiety and, by extension, support facial development and mouth-breathing correction, and some users pair it with mouth taping during sleep. Research has focused almost entirely on asthma, with small trials showing some improvement in symptoms and quality of life but little effect on lung function.

name: Rhinophyma laser / surgery

angle.text: Rhinophyma laser or surgical shaving is a recognised clinical treatment that removes the thickened tissue of advanced rosacea to restore a normal nose contour, with the change visible after healing. It is a medical procedure that appearance communities mention, not a looksmaxxing invention.

summary: Medical removal of the thickened, bulbous nasal tissue of advanced rosacea, usually by CO2 laser or surgical shaving; a recognised clinical procedure, not a looksmaxxing invention.
note: Rhinophyma is a medical condition; clinicians recommend biopsy because skin cancers can hide in thickened tissue.
currentQuick:
Rhinophyma is an advanced form of rosacea in which the skin of the lower nose thickens and enlarges, producing a bulbous, lumpy shape. Treatment for established cases is procedural: surgeons remove or reshape the excess tissue with a scalpel, electrosurgery, dermabrasion or an ablative carbon dioxide laser and let the nose heal over.
In looksmaxxing discussion it appears as one of the nose-related hardmaxxing procedures. Its medical literature is far older than the community, with a preliminary report on CO2 laser removal published in 1980.
How it works: The condition involves overgrowth of oil glands and fibrous connective tissue. Laser or surgical treatment removes the surplus tissue layer by layer so the nose can re-form a smoother contour, while rosacea itself is managed separately with topical or oral medicines.
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe scarring, pigment change, bleeding and recurrence as general concerns of any resurfacing or excision, and note that a biopsy is advised because basal cell carcinoma and other conditions can resemble or hide within rhinophyma. Procedures are performed by physicians and are prescription-level care.
deepLead:
Rhinophyma is a condition in which the nose becomes large and bulbous through thickening of the skin, enlargement of sebaceous glands and fibrous change. It is most often regarded as an advanced stage of rosacea and is most common in older men of European ancestry . Colloquial names include "whiskey nose" and "gin blossom", although the link with alcohol has not been established as causal .
Treatment of established rhinophyma is typically procedural. Clinical sources describe reducing the excess tissue with a sharp blade, electrosurgery, dermabrasion or a carbon dioxide laser, after which the area is left to re-epithelialise; in some cases the tissue is fully excised and grafted . A preliminary report on CO2 laser removal appeared in the medical literature in 1980 .
In looksmaxxing communities the topic sits among nose-related surgical and procedural options. The sources available for this article are medical rather than forum-based, and no published study evaluates the procedure as a looksmaxxing intervention.

name: Nasofrontal / nasolabial angle theory

chain: Choose surgery or jaw changes to fix
angle.text: Forum users borrow nasofrontal and nasolabial angle measurements from rhinoplasty and orthodontics to score side profiles and plan brow, nose or jaw changes. The angles are standard clinical measures, while the claim that they drive attractiveness comes mostly from community opinion.

summary: Profile-angle metrics borrowed from rhinoplasty and orthodontics that forums use to score noses and brow-to-nose transitions.
note: Published norms are clinical planning guides that vary by sex and population; forum cut-offs are informal.
currentQuick:
The nasofrontal angle is the angle at the nasion between the forehead and the nasal dorsum. The nasolabial angle is the angle between the columella and the upper lip under the nose. Both come from facial plastic surgery and orthodontic profile analysis, and looksmaxxing forums use them as shorthand for how a nose looks from the side.
Forum users discuss the angles in relation to brow ridge, nasal bridge height and tip rotation, and some ask about surgeries meant to alter them. Surgical texts give typical ranges that differ by sex.
How it works: This is a measurement framework rather than an intervention. The angles are read from a side-profile photo or X-ray, and users compare their values with published ranges. Changes are sought through rhinoplasty, brow-area implants or other procedures discussed elsewhere.
Risks and caveats: The framework itself carries no direct risk. Concerns noted in the literature are that ideal values vary between individuals, sexes and ethnic groups, and that interventions discussed in connection with the angles, such as surgery, carry their own risks.
deepLead:
The nasofrontal angle and the nasolabial angle are two measurements of the nose in side view. The nasofrontal angle sits at the nasion between the line along the forehead (nasion to glabella) and the line along the nasal dorsum, while the nasolabial angle is formed between the columella and the line from the subnasale to the upper lip .
In surgical references, the nasofrontal angle is usually given as about 115 to 130 degrees, more acute in men (about 115 to 120) than in women (about 120 to 130), and the nasolabial angle as roughly 90 to 95 degrees in men and 100 to 105 in women . These figures serve as planning guides rather than strict standards.
On looksmax.org and similar forums, the terms appear in threads about brow ridge projection, nasal bridge position and tip rotation, where users compare their own profiles with these ranges .

name: Rhinoplasty simulation apps

angle.text: Clinics and prospective patients use morphing and 3D imaging software to preview how a nose might look after surgery and to align expectations with the surgeon. The preview image is visible immediately. The actual surgical outcome is not guaranteed to match it.

summary: Morphing and 3D-imaging tools that preview how a nose might look after surgery; used by clinics and by prospective patients, with outcomes that are not guaranteed.
note: A simulated preview is an illustration, not a promise of surgical result.
currentQuick:
Rhinoplasty simulation software lets a person or a surgeon alter a photo or 3D scan of a nose to show a proposed change. Clinics use 3D cameras and planning software during consultations, and consumer apps offer similar photo morphing.
The topic appears in looksmaxxing discussion as a way to preview a result before surgery. This article is short because the available sources describe the clinical use only briefly.
How it works: Software maps the nose from standard photographs or 3D camera captures and lets the operator reshape contours digitally, so patient and surgeon can discuss the planned change.
Risks and caveats: The tools themselves are low-risk. The surgical result can differ from a simulation because healing, swelling and tissue behaviour vary between individuals; swelling after rhinoplasty can take a year or more to fully settle.
deepLead:
Rhinoplasty simulation refers to software that predicts or illustrates how a nose might look after surgery. Surgical references describe 3D simulations and 3D cameras that capture and analyse the nose, allow modifications, and help surgeon and patient understand the anatomy and preview a potential result .
Standard clinical practice also includes photographs from several angles before and after surgery, which supply the images these tools work from . Consumer apps that morph a photo exist alongside clinical systems, but the sources available for this article describe the clinical use only.
